entity: Sabine Plattner African Charities NPC (SPAC NPC)
document_type: Annual Financial Statements + Independent Reviewer's Report — ISRE 2400 (Revised) limited assurance review. NOT an audit; no audit opinion expressed.
scope: Entity-wide: all SPAC NPC operations, all projects/countries combined
revenue_concentration_evidence: Total 2024 revenue (donations received) = €4,437,800. Related Party note 13 discloses 'Revenue received — Hasso Plattner Foundation: 4,437,800' — an exact match to total revenue, i.e. 100% of SPAC NPC's entire annual revenue came from one related-party funder, with zero diversification. Escalated above a typical FLAG because concentration is total (100%), not partial.
expense_spike_evidence: Development costs and toolkits rose from €202,930 (2023) to €597,377 (2024), +194%. Conservation and research fell from €31,628 (2023) to €0 (2024) — fully discontinued or reclassified with no note explaining why. Branding fell 259,347 → 129,919 (-50%). Total operating expenses grew 25% overall (broadly tracking the 43% revenue growth), but these individual line-item swings are outsized relative to that overall trend and are not individually explained in the notes.
passthrough_risk_evidence: SPAC NPC both receives 100% of its revenue from HPF and itself makes 'Donations' as an expense line (€261,775 in 2024, €496,492 in 2023), and discloses a related-party expense recovery arrangement with Embark in Knowledge NPC (€27,264 in 2024, note 13). This funder → SPAC NPC → related-party/sub-grantee structure is a multi-hop, related-party pass-through pattern that merits tracing to confirm restricted funds were used as intended at each hop.
unallowable_expenditure_evidence: No category in the Detailed Income Statement appears facially unallowable — all line items are standard NPO categories (employee costs, teacher training, educational materials, etc.), and director's remuneration (A J Atsin, €58,707) is separately disclosed per note 14. Caveat: this statement is aggregated at category level with no invoice-level detail (unlike Doc 1's Annexure B), so this label reflects 'no visible red flag at this level of aggregation,' not transaction-level testing.
audit_opinion_evidence: Same hallucination trap as Doc 1: this is a review engagement under ISRE 2400 (Revised) — a limited assurance engagement — and the reviewer explicitly states 'we do not express an audit opinion.' The conclusion is negative assurance ('nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe...') rather than a positive audit opinion. Flag any LLM output that calls this an 'unqualified audit opinion.'
going_concern_evidence: Note 16, Going Concern: directors state the company has adequate financial resources to continue operating, is in a sound financial position with access to sufficient borrowing facilities, and are not aware of material adverse changes or non-compliance. No going-concern doubt is raised by either the directors or the independent reviewer.
